sections.heading: Project objective
sections.body:
Connect your website enquiries to HubSpot so the sales team can work from one reliable record instead of manually copying form submissions, sending an acknowledgement, and setting follow-up reminders. The initial scope covers your existing website form, HubSpot, Gmail, and Slack. The workflow will use n8n, with deterministic rules for record matching and task creation. AI is not necessary for the process described.
This proposal assumes a single enquiry form and one sales pipeline. The first review will confirm field names, record ownership, consent requirements, and the rule for deciding when a lead needs follow-up. Those decisions become the acceptance checklist before implementation begins.

sections.heading: Proposed approach
sections.body:
The form submission will trigger an n8n workflow that validates the required fields and looks for an existing HubSpot contact by email. A matching contact will be updated using agreed field rules; a new enquiry will create a contact. The implementation will preserve the source and submission identifier so repeated delivery of the same event can be recognized.
Once the CRM write succeeds, the workflow will send the approved acknowledgement through Gmail and create a HubSpot follow-up task for the assigned owner. Slack will receive a short operational notification with a link to the CRM record. Failed writes will not be treated as completed leads. Transient failures will have bounded retries, while unresolved errors will appear in an exception queue for review.
Before enabling live email, I would run the full flow against test contacts and a test mailbox. This allows your team to approve the message, task timing, and ownership behavior without sending trial acknowledgements to real prospects.

sections.heading: Deliverables and acceptance
bullets: One documented n8n workflow connecting the existing form, HubSpot, Gmail, and Slack. A valid test submission must produce the expected CRM record, acknowledgement, owner task, and notification.

Contact matching and duplicate-event protection. Replaying the same submission must not send another acknowledgement or create another follow-up task. A genuinely new enquiry from an existing contact must follow the agreed repeat-enquiry rule.
An exception path with enough context to investigate a failed run. Tests will cover missing required data and simulated service failures, including a recovery attempt after access is restored.
A short operating guide covering credentials, field mappings, workflow activation, exception handling, and safe changes. Handover includes a walkthrough using the delivered workflow.

sections.heading: Milestones and estimated schedule
sections.body: Allow approximately 5–7 working days after access and the acknowledgement copy are ready. This is a conditional estimate, not a confirmed start date. Client review time and any changes to the form integration can extend elapsed delivery time.
bullets: Discovery and mapping, approximately one working day: review a sample submission, confirm access, agree the duplicate and ownership rules, and record the acceptance cases.
Implementation, approximately two to three working days: build the workflow in a test setup, configure credential connections, and implement record handling and exception reporting.

Validation and handover, approximately two to three working days: run the agreed cases, incorporate one consolidated review of the in-scope behavior, enable the approved live workflow, and deliver the operating guide.

sections.heading: Dependencies and scope assumptions
sections.body:
You would provide access to the form integration, the relevant HubSpot account, the sending Gmail account, the Slack destination, and the n8n environment. Credentials should be configured through the platform's credential controls rather than copied into documents. Your team would approve the acknowledgement copy and confirm which contact fields the automation may overwrite.
This scope does not include rebuilding the website form, cleaning the entire historical CRM database, writing a multi-email nurture campaign, or changing your sales pipeline. If discovery identifies one of these as necessary, I would separate that work before changing the implementation scope. Subscription charges and any account limitations would be checked against your existing plans before launch.

sections.heading: Next step
sections.body:
Please share a sample form submission and the follow-up rule you want the sales team to use. With those two inputs, I can confirm the field mapping and whether the existing form supports the proposed trigger. Pricing can then be agreed against the confirmed scope.
Prepared by Aleem Ul Hassan. This is a synthetic test document for validating Upwork Proposal Studio, not a live client offer.
